accuracy_findings.claim: A pillage there takes its loot from your own credit, technology and ideology, not from the dominion. It takes the dominion's full output, even though you only receive a share of it.
accuracy_findings.problem: The added sentence "It takes the dominion's full output" can be read as "the loot equals one tick of the dominion's output". In the code, the loot is that output times 150 or 200 (by outcome), times the pillage yield divided by 100. The 8.1 verdict says "full output (times the pillage multiplier)". The behavior is described correctly, but the amount is loose.
accuracy_findings.fix: Reword so the loot is counted from the dominion's full output, for example: "The loot is counted on the dominion's full output, even though you only receive a share of it. See [[siege]] and [[dominion-tax-rate]]." The multiplier stays on siege and Navarch pages.
accuracy_findings.evidence: loot.ex:121-129 computes credit = system.credit.value * resources_multiplier * (siege_logs.raid_potential / 100), then {:add_resources, -credit, ...} on defender = system.owner, with multiplier 150 (normal success) or 200 (critical success). Script tmp/help-review/dominions-acc-r0-share.exs: with dominion credit 50 and yield 100, the owner loses 7.5e3 (normal) or 1.0e4 (critical), while the owner's share per tick is 15.0.

clarity_findings.claim: Rule 17 violation: "Every other mechanic named in the prose is a [[link]] the first time it appears" is broken for the mechanic "population."
clarity_findings.problem: In the "What you cannot do there" section the page reads: "You cannot order buildings or ships in a dominion. Its population gives it no [[defense]]." Defense is linked but "population" is not, even though population is a mechanic with its own guide page (priv/help/en/systems/population.md) and is not mentioned anywhere earlier on this page. Sibling pages in this same guide map follow the convention of linking population on first mention (e.g. the colonization brief: "...population. See [[population]]."), so the omission here is inconsistent with the rest of the category as well as with rule 17 itself.
clarity_findings.fix: Wrap the first occurrence in a link, e.g. "Its [[population]] gives it no [[defense]]."

clarity_findings.claim: The "Under attack" section half-explains the dominion-pillage mechanic instead of pointing to the page that owns it, violating style rule 4.
clarity_findings.problem: The section reads: "A Navarch can bombard or pillage your dominion. A pillage there takes loot based on the dominion's full output. You only receive a share of that output. But the loot comes out of your own credit, technology and ideology, not the dominion's. See [[siege]] and [[dominion-tax-rate]]." That is four sentences of explanation of how the pillage-of-a-dominion mechanic works (how much is taken, from whose stock, why the owner still only nets a share) before the pointer, which is exactly the pattern rule 4 forbids: "Point instead of half-explaining: 'See [[housing]].' beats a clause that summarizes housing... Bad: 'The housing factor turns growth negative once population passes housing + 0.75; the housing page explains how it behaves.'" This content is also outside the dominions guide's own brief: the guide map's OWNS list for `dominions` (guide-map-rest.md lines 297-301) has no item covering pillage-of-a-dominion, and the ownership matrix assigns the pillage-yield/outcome mechanics to `siege` and "per-outcome multipliers: Navarchs (Q4, Q5)" (line 433), while the credit/technology/ideology-share concept belongs to `dominion-tax-rate`. The very next sentence in the same page, "A dominion with negative output lowers your income. See [[dominion-tax-rate]].", shows the correct one-clause-then-point pattern for comparison.
clarity_findings.fix: Compress the pillage paragraph to one pointing sentence, e.g. "A Navarch can bombard or pillage your dominion, at your own cost. See [[siege]] and [[dominion-tax-rate]].", and let siege/dominion-tax-rate carry the detail of how the loot is computed and whose stock it draws from.
